claims.text: kube-scheduler places a Pod only on a node whose allocatable resources minus the sum of the requests of Pods already on it cover the Pod's requests; actual use by those Pods is not considered.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Resource Management for Pods and Containers > How Pods with resource requests are scheduled

claims.text: A container's request is reserved on its node whether used or not. A container with no request, no limit and no namespace default adds nothing to the scheduler's sum, though it still uses CPU and memory; a limit with no request, or a namespace (LimitRange) default, becomes the request.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Resource Management for Pods and Containers (requests, scheduling; limit copied as request); Limit Ranges (default requests)

claims.text: With a cluster autoscaler on a node pool, Pods whose requests fit no node lead it to add nodes, within the pool's configured maximum.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Node Autoscaling (provisioning triggered by unschedulable Pods); k8s.l4.node-autoscaling

claims.text: cluster-cost.md @ stage-4: nodes = sum of requests (CPU or memory, whichever needs more) / (one node's allocatable × target fill), rounded up; node 4 CPU / 8 GiB, fill 70%; cost in time, not money: node hours + 2 team days per cluster a month; all assumed.

cluster-cost.md 26-46 @ stage-4: only api sets requests (250m/256Mi per Pod, 2 replicas; total 500m/512Mi); others unset; proposed total 1720m/3264Mi, assumed because the lab has no metrics-server; manifests unchanged until measured at peak.

claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang STAGE.md @ stage-4 (clusters and their resources)

claims.text: Requests too low: under CPU contention CPU share follows the request, so the container is slowed; memory requests below use let the scheduler overpack a node, and under node memory pressure Pods using more than their requests are evicted first; too high: capacity no other Pod can use.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Resource Management for Pods and Containers (how requests are applied, CPU weight); Node-pressure Eviction (Pod selection: usage exceeding requests)

claims.text: With an HPA, the replica count falls toward minReplicas when load is low.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (minReplicas bound)

claims.text: Arithmetic from cluster-cost.md (proposed figures): platform 950m > 1/3 of 2670m; 70% of a node = 2800m / about 5734Mi; doubled workloads 3440m/6528Mi + platform = 4390m/8512Mi -> 2 nodes for CPU and for memory.

Opinion (trade-offs table): unset requests understate the node count and leave Pods no reserved share; generous requests overstate it and pay for idle capacity; rightsized requests need measured peak use first and leave only the chosen headroom idle.

Opinion: when unmeasured, cut staging cost by stopping it off-hours rather than writing guessed requests; put a fixed-replica api under an HPA when quiet hours hold idle replicas; for an extra demo environment, prefer a namespace unless it needs a separate cluster's boundary.
Kubernetes resource units: 1000m of CPU equals 1 CPU; Mi and Gi are binary units, so 1024Mi equals 1Gi.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Resource Management for Pods and Containers > Resource units in Kubernetes (CPU, memory)
